--- title: "Exercises – Week 2: Data Cleanup & Visualisation" --- ```{=html} ``` > 💡 The sandboxes use a **20-row sample** of the diabetes dataset. To work with the full dataset (400+ patients), load it in RStudio: > ```r > dat <- read.delim('https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/zqjdoi7naolmruyxrraxq/diabetes_2025.tsv?rlkey=txnps3ccr0vj47yvjmpecbeom&dl=1') > ``` --- :::: {.lang-r} ## Exercise Sheet — Data Exploration & Visualisation ### Exercise 1: Data Exploration and Summary Statistics The `summary()` function gives a quick overview, but sometimes you need more specific information. Using the diabetes dataset `dat`: 1. Calculate the **mean and standard deviation** of the `hdl` (High Density Lipoprotein) column using `mean()` and `sd()`. 2. Create a new column `bmi` using the formula: BMI = weight (lbs) / height² (in) × 703. Add it with `dat$bmi <- ...` 3. Use the `table()` function on the `location` column to count how many patients come from each location. Which location has the most patients? 4. Calculate the **median age** separately for male and female patients. Are they similar? ```{shinylive-r} #| standalone: true #| viewerHeight: 320 library(shiny) DAT <- data.frame( age = c(46,29,58,67,64,34,30,37,52,44,61,39,55,48,33,71,27,63,41,56), gender = c("female","female","female","male","male","female","male","male","female","male","male","female","male","female","male","female","male","male","female","male"), chol = c(203,165,228,259,294,155,170,205,218,192,275,148,240,201,189,262,158,281,175,233), hdl = c(56,42,63,48,45,71,53,55,60,44,52,68,47,58,49,62,65,43,72,51), weight = c(202,122,165,189,170,125,143,156,178,145,201,115,188,160,135,175,130,195,140,170), height = c(66,62,68,71,72,63,69,67,64,70,73,61,72,65,68,66,70,71,64,69), location = c("Louisa","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Buckingham") ) ui <- fluidPage( textAreaInput("code", NULL, value = "dat <- DAT\n", width = '100%', height = '160px'), actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"), verbatimTextOutput("out") ) server <- function(input, output) { observeEvent(input$run, { output$out <- renderPrint({ exprs <- parse(text = input$code) for (e in exprs) { res <- withVisible(eval(e)); if (!is.null(res$value) && res$visible) print(res$value) } }) }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` ```{=html} 
# Task 1 – mean and sd of hdl
mean(dat$hdl)
sd(dat$hdl)

# Task 2 – create bmi column
dat$bmi <- dat$weight / dat$height^2 * 703
head(dat$bmi)

# Task 3 – count patients per location
table(dat$location)

# Task 4 – median age by gender
median(dat$age[dat$gender == "male"])
median(dat$age[dat$gender == "female"])
``` --- ### Exercise 2: Visualising Relationships Between Variables Using the cleaned `dat` dataset, explore relationships between clinical measurements: 1. Create a **scatter plot** of `weight` vs `height` using `plot()`. Change the point style with `pch = 20`. 2. **Colour the points** by gender using the `col` parameter. *Hint: `col = as.factor(dat$gender)`*. Does the weight–height relationship differ between men and women? 3. Use `cor()` to calculate the **correlation coefficient** between `weight` and `height`. How strong is the relationship? 4. Create **side-by-side boxplots** of cholesterol by gender: `boxplot(chol ~ gender, data = dat)`. What differences do you observe? Try other variables! ```{shinylive-r} #| standalone: true #| viewerHeight: 440 library(shiny) DAT <- data.frame( age = c(46,29,58,67,64,34,30,37,52,44,61,39,55,48,33,71,27,63,41,56), gender = c("female","female","female","male","male","female","male","male","female","male","male","female","male","female","male","female","male","male","female","male"), chol = c(203,165,228,259,294,155,170,205,218,192,275,148,240,201,189,262,158,281,175,233), hdl = c(56,42,63,48,45,71,53,55,60,44,52,68,47,58,49,62,65,43,72,51), weight = c(202,122,165,189,170,125,143,156,178,145,201,115,188,160,135,175,130,195,140,170), height = c(66,62,68,71,72,63,69,67,64,70,73,61,72,65,68,66,70,71,64,69) ) ui <- fluidPage( textAreaInput("code", NULL, value = "dat <- DAT\n", width = '100%', height = '130px'), actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"), plotOutput("plot", height = "260px") ) server <- function(input, output) { observeEvent(input$run, { output$plot <- renderPlot({ dat <- DAT exprs <- parse(text = input$code) for (e in exprs) eval(e) }) }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` ```{=html} 
# Task 1 – scatter plot
plot(dat$height, dat$weight, pch = 20,
     xlab = "Height (in)", ylab = "Weight (lbs)")

# Task 2 – colour by gender
plot(dat$height, dat$weight, pch = 20,
     col = as.factor(dat$gender),
     xlab = "Height (in)", ylab = "Weight (lbs)")
legend("topleft", legend = levels(as.factor(dat$gender)),
       col = 1:2, pch = 20)

# Task 3 – correlation
cor(dat$weight, dat$height)

# Task 4 – boxplots by gender
boxplot(chol ~ gender, data = dat,
        main = "Cholesterol by Gender", ylab = "Cholesterol (mg/dL)")
``` --- ### Going Further: Advanced Data Manipulation ⭐ These tasks are more challenging and work best with the full dataset in RStudio. 1. Create a categorical variable `age_group` that classifies patients as `"young"` (age < 40), `"middle"` (40 ≤ age < 60), or `"senior"` (age ≥ 60). Add it as a new column to `dat`. *Hint: use the `cut()` function.* 2. Calculate the **mean cholesterol** for each combination of `gender` and `age_group`. *Hint: `tapply(dat$chol, list(dat$gender, dat$age_group), mean)`* 3. Write a function `standardize()` that takes a numeric vector and returns its **z-score** (subtract mean, divide by sd). Apply it to all numeric columns in `dat` to create `dat.scaled`. *Hint: `apply()` with `MARGIN = 2`, skip non-numeric columns.* 4. Using `dat.scaled`, identify which patient has the most **extreme standardised BMI** (highest or lowest). Print all their clinical information. ```{shinylive-r} #| standalone: true #| viewerHeight: 340 library(shiny) DAT <- data.frame( age = c(46,29,58,67,64,34,30,37,52,44,61,39,55,48,33,71,27,63,41,56), gender = c("female","female","female","male","male","female","male","male","female","male","male","female","male","female","male","female","male","male","female","male"), chol = c(203,165,228,259,294,155,170,205,218,192,275,148,240,201,189,262,158,281,175,233), hdl = c(56,42,63,48,45,71,53,55,60,44,52,68,47,58,49,62,65,43,72,51), weight = c(202,122,165,189,170,125,143,156,178,145,201,115,188,160,135,175,130,195,140,170), height = c(66,62,68,71,72,63,69,67,64,70,73,61,72,65,68,66,70,71,64,69) ) DAT$bmi <- DAT$weight / DAT$height^2 * 703 ui <- fluidPage( textAreaInput("code", NULL, value = "dat <- DAT\n# dat already has a bmi column\n", width = '100%', height = '170px'), actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"), verbatimTextOutput("out") ) server <- function(input, output) { observeEvent(input$run, { output$out <- renderPrint({ dat <- DAT exprs <- parse(text = input$code) for (e in exprs) { res <- withVisible(eval(e)); if (!is.null(res$value) && res$visible) print(res$value) } }) }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` ```{=html} 
# Task 1 – age_group
dat$age_group <- cut(dat$age,
                     breaks = c(0, 40, 60, Inf),
                     labels = c("young", "middle", "senior"),
                     right  = FALSE)

# Task 2 – mean chol by gender × age_group
tapply(dat$chol, list(dat$gender, dat$age_group), mean)

# Task 3 – standardize function
standardize <- function(x) (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)

numeric_cols <- sapply(dat, is.numeric)
dat.scaled <- dat
dat.scaled[, numeric_cols] <- apply(dat[, numeric_cols], 2, standardize)

# Task 4 – most extreme standardised BMI
extreme_idx <- which.max(abs(dat.scaled$bmi))
dat[extreme_idx, ]
``` --- ## Plenum Questions ### Question 1: Which measure of spread is most robust to outliers? Create two datasets — one clean and one with three extreme outliers added. For both, compute the following spread measures and compare how much they change: - Standard deviation (`sd()`) - 10%–90% quantile spread (`quantile()`) - MAD (`mad()`) - Range (`max() - min()`) Which measure changes the least when outliers are added? ```{shinylive-r} #| standalone: true #| viewerHeight: 300 library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( textAreaInput("code", NULL, value = "set.seed(123)\ndata1 <- rnorm(100, mean = 50, sd = 5)\ndata2 <- c(data1, 80, 100, 120)\n", width = '100%', height = '140px'), actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"), verbatimTextOutput("out") ) server <- function(input, output) { observeEvent(input$run, { output$out <- renderPrint({ exprs <- parse(text = input$code) for (e in exprs) { res <- withVisible(eval(e)); if (!is.null(res$value) && res$visible) print(res$value) } }) }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` ```{=html} 
set.seed(123)
data1 <- rnorm(100, mean = 50, sd = 5)
data2 <- c(data1, 80, 100, 120)

# Measures without outliers
measures1 <- c(
  SD     = sd(data1),
  Spread = as.numeric(quantile(data1, 0.9) - quantile(data1, 0.1)),
  MAD    = mad(data1),
  Range  = max(data1) - min(data1)
)

# Measures with outliers
measures2 <- c(
  SD     = sd(data2),
  Spread = as.numeric(quantile(data2, 0.9) - quantile(data2, 0.1)),
  MAD    = mad(data2),
  Range  = max(data2) - min(data2)
)

rbind(Without_outliers = measures1,
      With_outliers    = measures2)
``` --- ### Question 2: How do Mode, Median, and Mean relate in differently shaped distributions? For three theoretical distributions — symmetric (Normal), right-skewed (Exponential), and left-skewed (Beta) — create line plots that include vertical lines for the **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode**. What pattern do you observe about the order of these three measures depending on the direction of the skew? ```{shinylive-r} #| standalone: true #| viewerHeight: 560 library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( textAreaInput("code", NULL, value = "# Distribution parameters:\n# Symmetric: Normal(mean=100, sd=15)\n# Right-skewed: Exponential(rate=1/50)\n# Left-skewed: Beta(shape1=5, shape2=2) × 100\n", width = '100%', height = '110px'), actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"), plotOutput("plot", height = "400px") ) server <- function(input, output) { observeEvent(input$run, { output$plot <- renderPlot({ exprs <- parse(text = input$code) for (e in exprs) eval(e) }) }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` ```{=html} 
par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 2))

# 1. Symmetric (Normal)
sym_x <- seq(40, 160, length.out = 1000)
sym_y <- dnorm(sym_x, mean = 100, sd = 15)
plot(sym_x, sym_y, type = "l", col = "steelblue", lwd = 2,
     main = "Symmetric (Normal)", xlab = "Value", ylab = "Density")
abline(v = 100, col = "red",    lwd = 2, lty = 1)  # mean
abline(v = 100, col = "green",  lwd = 2, lty = 2)  # median
abline(v = 100, col = "orange", lwd = 2, lty = 3)  # mode
legend("topright", c("Mean","Median","Mode"),
       col = c("red","green","orange"), lty = 1:3, lwd = 2, cex = 0.8)

# 2. Right-skewed (Exponential)
right_x      <- seq(0, 300, length.out = 1000)
right_y      <- dexp(right_x, rate = 1/50)
right_mean   <- 50
right_median <- 50 * log(2)
right_mode   <- 0
plot(right_x, right_y, type = "l", col = "steelblue", lwd = 2,
     main = "Right-Skewed (Exponential)", xlab = "Value", ylab = "Density")
abline(v = right_mean,   col = "red",    lwd = 2, lty = 1)
abline(v = right_median, col = "green",  lwd = 2, lty = 2)
abline(v = right_mode,   col = "orange", lwd = 2, lty = 3)
legend("topright", c("Mean","Median","Mode"),
       col = c("red","green","orange"), lty = 1:3, lwd = 2, cex = 0.8)

# 3. Left-skewed (Beta × 100)
left_x      <- seq(0, 100, length.out = 1000)
left_y      <- dbeta(left_x / 100, shape1 = 5, shape2 = 2) / 100
left_mean   <- (5 / (5 + 2)) * 100
left_median <- qbeta(0.5, 5, 2) * 100
left_mode   <- ((5 - 1) / (5 + 2 - 2)) * 100
plot(left_x, left_y, type = "l", col = "steelblue", lwd = 2,
     main = "Left-Skewed (Beta)", xlab = "Value", ylab = "Density")
abline(v = left_mean,   col = "red",    lwd = 2, lty = 1)
abline(v = left_median, col = "green",  lwd = 2, lty = 2)
abline(v = left_mode,   col = "orange", lwd = 2, lty = 3)
legend("topleft", c("Mean","Median","Mode"),
       col = c("red","green","orange"), lty = 1:3, lwd = 2, cex = 0.8)
``` --- ### Question 4: Mean–Variance relationship in gene expression data Simulate expression counts for 200 genes across 10 samples using a negative binomial distribution (common for RNA-seq data). Plot the **mean expression** against the **variance** per gene. Add a reference line for the Poisson expectation (variance = mean). What do you observe? ```{shinylive-r} #| standalone: true #| viewerHeight: 440 library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( textAreaInput("code", NULL, value = "set.seed(123)\nn_genes <- 200\nn_samples <- 10\ngene_means <- runif(n_genes, min = 1, max = 100)\n", width = '100%', height = '120px'), actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"), plotOutput("plot", height = "280px") ) server <- function(input, output) { observeEvent(input$run, { output$plot <- renderPlot({ exprs <- parse(text = input$code) for (e in exprs) eval(e) }) }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` ```{=html} 
set.seed(123)
n_genes   <- 200
n_samples <- 10
gene_means <- runif(n_genes, min = 1, max = 100)

# Simulate expression matrix (negative binomial)
expr_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = n_genes, ncol = n_samples)
for (i in 1:n_genes) {
  expr_mat[i, ] <- rnbinom(n_samples, mu = gene_means[i], size = 5)
}

mean_expr <- rowMeans(expr_mat)
var_expr  <- apply(expr_mat, 1, var)

plot(mean_expr, var_expr,
     xlab = "Mean Expression", ylab = "Variance",
     main = "Mean-Variance Relationship in Gene Expression",
     pch = 16, col = "blue")
abline(a = 0, b = 1,    col = "red",   lty = 2, lwd = 2)  # Poisson
abline(lm(var_expr ~ mean_expr), col = "green", lwd = 2)   # actual trend
legend("topleft",
       legend = c("Genes", "Poisson (Var=Mean)", "Actual trend"),
       col = c("blue", "red", "green"), pch = c(16, NA, NA),
       lty = c(NA, 2, 1), lwd = c(NA, 2, 2))
``` --- ### Question 5: When do standard boxplots fail? Create four datasets with different characteristics (normal, bimodal, small n, skewed). First plot them as standard boxplots — what information is hidden? Then add jittered individual points on top. What do the improved plots reveal that the plain boxplots missed? ```{shinylive-r} #| standalone: true #| viewerHeight: 520 library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( textAreaInput("code", NULL, value = "set.seed(123)\ndata1 <- rnorm(100, mean = 50, sd = 10) # Normal\ndata2 <- c(rnorm(50, mean = 40, sd = 3),\n rnorm(50, mean = 60, sd = 3)) # Bimodal\ndata3 <- rnorm(20, mean = 50, sd = 10) # Small n\ndata4 <- rgamma(100, shape = 2, rate = 0.04) # Skewed\n", width = '100%', height = '145px'), actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"), plotOutput("plot", height = "320px") ) server <- function(input, output) { observeEvent(input$run, { output$plot <- renderPlot({ exprs <- parse(text = input$code) for (e in exprs) eval(e) }) }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` ```{=html} 
set.seed(123)
data1 <- rnorm(100, mean = 50, sd = 10)
data2 <- c(rnorm(50, mean = 40, sd = 3), rnorm(50, mean = 60, sd = 3))
data3 <- rnorm(20,  mean = 50, sd = 10)
data4 <- rgamma(100, shape = 2, rate = 0.04)

par(mfrow = c(2, 4), mar = c(3, 3, 3, 1))

# Row 1: Standard boxplots
boxplot(data1, main = "Normal (n=100)",  ylim = c(20, 80))
boxplot(data2, main = "Bimodal (n=100)", ylim = c(20, 80))
boxplot(data3, main = "Normal (n=20)",   ylim = c(20, 80))
boxplot(data4, main = "Skewed (n=100)",  ylim = c(20, 80))

# Row 2: Boxplots + jittered points
boxplot(data1, main = "Normal + points", ylim = c(20, 80))
points(jitter(rep(1, 100), 0.2), data1, col = rgb(0,0,1,0.4), pch = 16, cex = 0.6)

boxplot(data2, main = "Bimodal revealed!", ylim = c(20, 80))
points(jitter(rep(1, 100), 0.2), data2, col = rgb(1,0,0,0.4), pch = 16, cex = 0.6)

boxplot(data3, main = "Small n visible", ylim = c(20, 80))
points(jitter(rep(1, 20),  0.2), data3, col = rgb(0,0,0,0.6), pch = 16, cex = 0.6)

boxplot(data4, main = "Skew visible", ylim = c(20, 80))
points(jitter(rep(1, 100), 0.2), data4, col = rgb(0.5,0,0.5,0.4), pch = 16, cex = 0.6)
``` :::: --- :::: {.lang-python} ## Exercise Sheet — Data Exploration & Visualisation ### Exercise 1: Data Exploration and Summary Statistics The `.describe()` method gives a quick overview, but sometimes you need more targeted statistics. Using the diabetes dataset `dat`: 1. Calculate the **mean and standard deviation** of the `hdl` column using `.mean()` and `.std()`. 2. Create a new column `bmi` using the formula: BMI = weight (lbs) / height² (in) × 703. Use `dat['bmi'] = ...` 3. Use `.value_counts()` on the `location` column to count patients per location. Which location has more patients? 4. Calculate the **median age** separately for male and female patients using `.groupby()`. Are they similar? ```{shinylive-python} #| standalone: true #| viewerHeight: 320 from shiny import App, ui, render, reactive import io, contextlib, ast import numpy as np import pandas as pd DAT = pd.DataFrame({ 'age': [46,29,58,67,64,34,30,37,52,44,61,39,55,48,33,71,27,63,41,56], 'gender': ['female','female','female','male','male','female','male','male','female','male','male','female','male','female','male','female','male','male','female','male'], 'chol': [203,165,228,259,294,155,170,205,218,192,275,148,240,201,189,262,158,281,175,233], 'hdl': [56,42,63,48,45,71,53,55,60,44,52,68,47,58,49,62,65,43,72,51], 'weight': [202,122,165,189,170,125,143,156,178,145,201,115,188,160,135,175,130,195,140,170], 'height': [66,62,68,71,72,63,69,67,64,70,73,61,72,65,68,66,70,71,64,69], 'location': ['Louisa','Louisa','Buckingham','Louisa','Buckingham','Louisa','Buckingham','Louisa','Buckingham','Louisa','Buckingham','Louisa','Buckingham','Louisa','Louisa','Buckingham','Louisa','Buckingham','Louisa','Buckingham'] }) app_ui = ui.page_fluid( ui.input_text_area("code", None, value="dat = DAT.copy()\n", width='100%', height='160px'), ui.input_action_button("run", "Run Code", class_="btn-success"), ui.output_text_verbatim("out") ) def server(input, output, session): @render.text @reactive.event(input.run) async def out(): f = io.StringIO() ns = {"np": np, "pd": pd, "DAT": DAT} with contextlib.redirect_stdout(f): try: tree = ast.parse(input.code()) for node in tree.body: if isinstance(node, ast.Expr): val = eval(compile(ast.Expression(node.value),'','eval'), ns) if val is not None: print(val) else: exec(compile(ast.Module([node],[]),'','exec'), ns) except Exception as e: print(f"Error: {e}") return f.getvalue() app = App(app_ui, server) ``` ```{=html}

Try other variables! ```{shinylive-python} #| standalone: true #| viewerHeight: 440 from shiny import App, ui, render, reactive import ast import numpy as np import pandas as pd import matplotlib matplotlib.use('Agg') import matplotlib.pyplot as plt DAT = pd.DataFrame({ 'age': [46,29,58,67,64,34,30,37,52,44,61,39,55,48,33,71,27,63,41,56], 'gender': ['female','female','female','male','male','female','male','male','female','male','male','female','male','female','male','female','male','male','female','male'], 'chol': [203,165,228,259,294,155,170,205,218,192,275,148,240,201,189,262,158,281,175,233], 'hdl': [56,42,63,48,45,71,53,55,60,44,52,68,47,58,49,62,65,43,72,51], 'weight': [202,122,165,189,170,125,143,156,178,145,201,115,188,160,135,175,130,195,140,170], 'height': [66,62,68,71,72,63,69,67,64,70,73,61,72,65,68,66,70,71,64,69] }) app_ui = ui.page_fluid( ui.input_text_area("code", None, value="dat = DAT.copy()\n", width='100%', height='130px'), ui.input_action_button("run", "Run Code", class_="btn-success"), ui.output_plot("plot", height="260px") ) def server(input, output, session): @render.plot @reactive.event(input.run) def plot(): plt.clf() ns = {"np": np, "pd": pd, "plt": plt, "DAT": DAT} try: exec(input.code(), ns) except Exception as e: plt.text(0.5, 0.5, f"Error: {e}", ha='center', va='center') app = App(app_ui, server) ``` ```{=html}

Create a categorical column `age_group` classifying patients as `"young"` (age < 40), `"middle"` (40 ≤ age < 60), or `"senior"` (age ≥ 60). Use `pd.cut()`. 2. Calculate **mean cholesterol** for each combination of `gender` and `age_group` using `.groupby()`. 3.     }, name=label)

Plot the **mean expression** against the **variance** per gene. Add a reference line for the Poisson expectation (variance = mean). What do you observe? ```{shinylive-python} #| standalone: true #| viewerHeight: 440 from shiny import App, ui, render, reactive import ast import numpy as np import matplotlib matplotlib.use('Agg') import matplotlib.pyplot as plt app_ui = ui.page_fluid( ui.input_text_area("code", None, value="np.random.seed(123)\nn_genes = 200\nn_samples = 10\ngene_means = np.random.uniform(1, 100, n_genes)\n", width='100%', height='120px'), ui.input_action_button("run", "Run Code", class_="btn-success"), ui.output_plot("plot", height="280px") ) def server(input, output, session): @render.plot @reactive.event(input.run) def plot(): plt.clf() ns = {"np": np, "plt": plt} try: exec(input.code(), ns) except Exception as e: plt.text(0.5, 0.5, f"Error: {e}", ha='center', va='center') app = App(app_ui, server) ``` ```{=html} 
np.random.seed(123)
n_genes   = 200
n_samples = 10
gene_means = np.random.uniform(1, 100, n_genes)

# Simulate expression matrix (negative binomial)
size = 5
expr_mat = np.zeros((n_genes, n_samples))
for i in range(n_genes):
    mu = gene_means[i]
    p  = size / (size + mu)
    expr_mat[i, :] = np.random.negative_binomial(size, p, n_samples)

mean_expr = expr_mat.mean(axis=1)
var_expr  = expr_mat.var(axis=1, ddof=1)

plt.scatter(mean_expr, var_expr, color='blue', alpha=0.6, s=20)
plt.plot([0, mean_expr.max()], [0, mean_expr.max()],
         'r--', lw=2, label='Poisson (Var = Mean)')
m, b = np.polyfit(mean_expr, var_expr, 1)
x_fit = np.linspace(0, mean_expr.max(), 200)
plt.plot(x_fit, m*x_fit + b, 'g-', lw=2, label='Actual trend')
plt.xlabel('Mean Expression')
plt.ylabel('Variance')
plt.title('Mean–Variance Relationship in Gene Expression')
plt.legend()
